newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB's Tractebel buy would not alter control.
newsitem.headline: SGB's Tractebel buy would not alter control.

text.p: A possible acquisition by Belgian Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) of shares in utility holding company Tractebel SA would not alter de facto control over Tractebel, Tractebel said.
"The fact that SGB would possibly buy shares in Tractebel would not involve a change of control," a Tractebel spokesman said.

SGB, which has a 40.5 percent direct and indirect Tractebel stake, already is the leading shareholder. Analysts expect SGB to announce an acquisition of more Tractebel stock from Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL) later today.
GBL unit Electrafina holds 20.3 percent of Tractebel. Insurance company Royale Belge SA, another GBL affiliate, owns 4.3 percent.

Under Belgian takeover law a company which buys a large block of shares in another listed company is only obliged to make a full bid for all outstanding shares of the target company if its offer price is above the market price and the acquisition changes shareholder control over the target company.
Belgian media have speculated on whether SGB would be obliged to bid for all of Tractebel's stock if it acquired a sizeable block from GBL's affiliates.

"The main question is price. Perhaps the agreed takeover price is not the previously reported 14,500 francs, but maybe a figure closer to 14,000 francs per share," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
He added the press leak about the planned operation on September 3 may have been deliberate in order to inflate the market price to 14,500 francs per share.
"This would prop up Tractebel's price, which the market would quote at a discount to 14,500 francs, but would put a true price of about 14,000 francs well within reach," he said.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
